103: Termination policy type = Bandit and parameter = slack_factor. Bandit compares each run's primary metric against the best-performing run using a slack allowance, so setting slack_factor to 0.25 terminates runs that fall 25 percent or more below the best. Median stopping and truncation selection do not compare against the best run using a slack, and max_value/truncation_percentage are the wrong parameters.

The evaluation dataset is already registered, so uploading data is not needed.
150: Correct order: 1) Register the fine-tuned model version, 2) Evaluate and validate the model, 3) Create a Global Standard deployment. Promotion to production first requires versioning the fine-tuned model in the registry so it is tracked and immutable, then validating it against quality/safety criteria before release, and finally deploying it on a production-grade Global Standard deployment. A Developer Tier deployment is intended for experimentation, not production, so it is not used for the promotion path.
151: Domain specialization -> Supervised fine-tuning: teaching the model specialized domain knowledge/behavior is best achieved by fine-tuning on labeled domain examples. Poor response accuracy of a RAG-based solution -> Apply prompt engineering: the first, cheapest and fastest lever for a RAG solution is to improve the prompt (grounding instructions, context formatting) before resorting to tuning temperature/max_tokens or retraining.
152: The number of tokens used by each LLM node -> Traces: traces capture per-node execution details including token consumption for each LLM call in the flow. The accuracy of the model -> Metrics: evaluation metrics (such as accuracy) are produced by the evaluation/metrics output, not by traces or logs.
153: Correct order: 1) Generate a Secure Shell (SSH) key pair, 2) Add a public key to account1, 3) Create a compute instance, 4) Open a terminal window. To maximize clone performance you use SSH (not HTTPS): first generate the key pair, register the PUBLIC key with the GitHub account (the private key stays on the client), then create the compute instance that will host the clone, and finally open its terminal to run git clone with the SSH URL. Adding a private key to GitHub would be a security error.
154: Provide expected results for metric comparison -> Reference dataset: a reference (ground-truth) dataset supplies the expected 'golden' outputs needed to score generated responses. Align model responses to evaluation fields -> Output mapping: output mapping maps parts of the model response to the evaluation fields so structured metrics can be computed consistently. Ensure results are comparable across runs -> Consistent test dataset: using the exact same fixed inputs each run ensures metric changes reflect model/app changes rather than test-data variation.
157: Store secrets securely -> Azure Key Vault: an AML workspace uses an associated Key Vault to securely store secrets, keys and connection strings. Collect logs and metrics -> Azure Application Insights: the workspace's associated Application Insights resource captures operational logs, metrics and telemetry for monitoring.
158: Define how features are retrieved at inference -> Feature retrieval specification: it declares which features/feature sets to fetch at inference time. Ensure feature consistency between training and inference -> Feature set asset: the registered feature set asset holds the shared feature definitions used both in training and serving, preventing training/serving skew. Enable automated feature lookup in production -> Feature retrieval specification: packaging the retrieval spec with the model lets the deployed endpoint automatically look up the same features without manual configuration.
160: Significant change in input data distribution -> Investigate data drift: a shift in the input distribution is the definition of data drift, so investigate it. Sustained drop in prediction accuracy -> Trigger model retraining: persistent quality degradation indicates the model is stale and should be retrained. Sudden increase in endpoint error rate -> Inspect endpoint logs and health: a spike in errors is an operational/serving problem, so examine the endpoint logs and health rather than the model itself.
